critical.issue: Payment to a supplier is applied TWICE: create_purchase increments purchases.paid by 'take' AND inserts a supplier_payments doc; then supplier_owed() computes owed = opening + Σ(total-paid) − Σ(supplier_payments.amount) → the payment is subtracted twice. Repro: create supplier, record purchase total=500 paid=0 (owed=500), POST /api/supplier-payments amount=200 → supplier profile now returns owed=100 instead of 300. Reference: /app/backend/routes/purchases.py:65-73 (supplier_owed) and 160-167 (pay_supplier updates purchases.paid). Fix options: (a) drop the purchases.paid $inc and derive due from Σ payments only, or (b) drop the '− Σ supplier_payments' term in supplier_owed. Same double-count will also inflate the aggregate 'owed' on GET /api/suppliers and skew /api/reports/receivables.payables.

rca_of_issue: supplier_owed double-count: pay_supplier() FIFO-applies the payment onto purchases.paid AND inserts a supplier_payments record. supplier_owed() then reads BOTH: sums (total-paid) across purchases (which already reflects the payment) AND subtracts the amount from supplier_payments. Net effect: every payment reduces the visible owed by 2x its amount. Reproduction: POST /api/suppliers {name:X} → POST /api/purchases {supplier_id, lines=[{item_id, quantity:1, unit_cost:500}], paid:0} → GET /api/suppliers/{id} shows owed=500 → POST /api/supplier-payments {amount:200} → GET again shows owed=100 (expected 300). Mitigation: pick a single source of truth — recommend removing the '- Σ supplier_payments.amount' term from supplier_owed since pay_supplier already increments purchases.paid; alternately, store payments only in supplier_payments and derive purchase.due = purchase.total − Σ(payments_allocated_to_this_purchase).
